text:
carmen: Heads up — I found a partial service account JSON in a public gist (link removed). The private_key field looked truncated but the key ID matches a staging SA used by the image builder. I removed the gist.
security-oncall: Thanks. Initiating triage. Treat as compromised until we know otherwise. Carmen, can you paste the SA email and last 8 chars of the key id?
carmen: sa-image-builder-staging@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com
key last 8: 9a7f3c2b
Also saw a build log reference to a vault-unwrap job that used that SA.
ben: On it — listing keys for that SA now. Command:
```
gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=sa-image-builder-staging@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com --format=json
```
Found 2 keys: key-A (2025-10-01) and key-B (2026-03-01).
alice: Immediate plan:
1) revoke/delete the exposed keys
2) rotate any Vault/KMS bindings that used that SA
3) tighten RBAC for who can create SA keys
4) enable KMS/IAM audit logs and capture access
Assign owners and tickets.
security-oncall: Ben -> delete both keys and create a fresh key if the pipeline needs one. Open an incident ticket and add timeline. Carmen -> enumerate jobs using the SA. Alice -> push a temporary IAM restriction to block non-sre groups from creating SA keys for 1 hour.
ben: Deleted both keys. Commands used:
```
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete KEY_ID --iam-account=sa-image-builder-staging@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
Created a new key and stored it in Secret Manager for the builder pipeline, then rotated the pipeline to pick the new secret.
sre-op: Deployed pipeline config to use Secret Manager and workload identity binding instead of stored JSON keys. Test build succeeded.
alice: Pushed temporary IAM policy to restrict key creation (will auto-revert in 2 hours). Also created a Logging sink to capture KMS/IAM events to BigQuery for forensic analysis. Example sink command we used:
```
gcloud logging sinks create sink-kms-bq bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/redwood-ops/datasets/kms_audit --log-filter='protoPayload.methodName:"google.cloud.kms" OR protoPayload.serviceName:"iam.googleapis.com"'
```
security-oncall: We also need to rewrap any Vault transit/data keys that were provisioned or unsealed with that SA principal. Triggering rewrap and rotation now. Steps:
```
# trigger vault transit rotation
vault write sys/rotate-transit-key name=redwood-transit
# verify KMS key versions
gcloud kms keys versions list --key=redwood-kms --location=global
```
I triggered a KMS rewrap for the Vault data key using Cloud KMS rewrap API.
vault-bot: Rewrap job started for transit/redwood-transit at 1768501300. Status: in_progress.
carmen: Do we need to re-encrypt KV v2 secrets that referenced that transit key, or will rewrap handle it? I can scan mounts referencing transit/redwood-transit.
alice: Rewrap of the transit key should preserve ciphertext but re-encrypt the wrapped DEK. Still run smoke reads. Do a `vault kv get` for a handful of secrets in staging to verify.
ben: Smoke checks done, 5/5 reads successful. Also exported IAM/KMS audit logs for the timeframe around the leak.
security-oncall: Incident INC-3891 opened with timeline, keys deleted, RBAC restriction, audit sink creation, rewrap job id 42, and owners. Postmortem owner: carmen. Action items: rotate all SA keys older than 90 days, accelerate rollout of Workload Identity, remove SA key creation from engineering groups, add an automated scanner for public gists that match our domain.
carmen: Acknowledged — I'll draft the postmortem and post to eng-security for review. Thanks for the quick responses everyone :heart:
